topic: nRF5340 PWM, TIMER and DPPI for ADC-PWM synchronisation
citation: Nordic Semiconductor. nRF5340 Product Specification v1.6 (Feb 2025): PWM, DPPI chapters; Current consumption
key_quantitative_findings: PWM: 4 instances (PWM0-3) x 4 channels, one common 15-bit counter (COUNTERTOP up to 32767), up mode (edge-aligned) or up-and-down (centre-aligned); T_PWM(Up) = T_PWM_CLK x COUNTERTOP, T_PWM(UpDown) = 2 x T_PWM_CLK x COUNTERTOP; compare values loaded from RAM by EasyDMA sequences (previous value repeated if EasyDMA cannot update within the period); PWM clock 16 MHz max (current table: 'PWM running at 16 MHz' 560 uA). DPPI: 32 channels and 6 channel groups per domain; one-to-many and many-to-one event-task links without CPU. TIMER: three 32-bit timers with counter mode (key features); current table lists 'One TIMER running @ 16 MHz' (560 uA). [calc] 20 kHz PWM: 800 counts (9.6 bit) edge-aligned, 400 counts (8.6 bit) centre-aligned; 10 kHz: 1600 / 800 counts (10.6 / 9.6 bit).
units_and_conditions: PWM/TIMER clock 16 MHz; currents at 3 V, DC/DC
locator: PS v1.6 > PWM (pwm.html: counter, modes, SEQ[n], SUBSCRIBE/PUBLISH registers); DPPI (dppi.html); Current consumption (IPWM,RUN1; ITIMER2)

topic: CMSIS-NN version, operators, data types and ISA requirements
citation: Arm. CMSIS-NN software library: GitHub ARM-software/CMSIS-NN README (main); release v8.0.0 notes; Keil CMSIS-NN pack versions page
key_quantitative_findings: Latest release 8.0.0 (Keil pack dated 21 Aug 2026; previous 7.0.0 27 Nov 2024, 6.0.0 3 Jun 2024); two releases per year planned; Apache-2.0. Follows the TFLM int8 and int16 quantization specification and is bit-exact with TFLM reference kernels. Implementations selected by compiler feature flags: pure C (e.g., Cortex-M0/M3), DSP extension SIMD (e.g., Cortex-M4 or Cortex-M33 configured with DSP), MVE/Helium (Cortex-M55/M85). Operator table: Conv2D, DepthwiseConv2D, Fully Connected, Batch MatMul, Add, Mul, Max/AvgPool, Softmax, LSTM in C and DSP paths for int8 and int16 (int4 weights with int8 activations for Conv2D/DW/FC); TransposeConv2D and SVDF int8 only; Pad, Transpose, Min, Max without DSP path. v8.0.0: experimental float16/float32 operator APIs (opt-in ARM_NN_ENABLE_F16/F32, MVE-targeted), optimised arm_nn_requantize for Thumb-2, LSTM state-persistence fixes, Python bindings for buffer-size functions.

topic: CMSIS-NN convolution dispatch and dilation support (source inspection)
citation: Arm. CMSIS-NN source (main): arm_convolve_wrapper_s8.c V.2.5.2 (27 Feb 2026); arm_nnsupportfunctions.h (arm_nn_is_convolve_1_x_n); arm_convolve_s8.c V.4.0.0 (4 Nov 2024); arm_depthwise_conv_wrapper_s8.c V.2.2.1 (17 Jan 2025); arm_depthwise_conv_s8.c V.3.1.0 (22 Sep 2026)

key_quantitative_findings: arm_convolve_wrapper_s8: 1x1 -> arm_convolve_1x1_s8(_fast); 1xN fast path arm_convolve_1_x_n_s8 only if input h == 1 AND dilation.w == 1 AND filter h == 1 AND (stride.w x C_in) % 4 == 0 AND C_in == filter C; otherwise generic arm_convolve_s8 (partial im2col + GEMM), which implements dilation_x/dilation_y. DSP path widens int8 to int16 with the input offset and runs a GEMM on two im2col columns at a time; source note: optimal 'when input and output channels are multiples of 4'. Depthwise wrapper uses 3x3/opt kernels only when dilation = 1 (and ch_mult = 1, batch 1), else generic arm_depthwise_conv_s8, which implements dilation (header comments saying 'dilation is not used' are stale).

topic: CMSIS-NN published kernel performance (original paper)
citation: Lai L, Suda N, Chandra V. CMSIS-NN: Efficient Neural Network Kernels for Arm Cortex-M CPUs. arXiv:1801.06601v1, 19 Jan 2018 (Arm technical report, not peer reviewed)
task_or_setup: CIFAR-10 CNN (3 x conv 5x5 + max-pool + FC), 8-bit fixed point
key_quantitative_findings: Total 24.7 M ops, 87 kB weights, 55 kB activations: 99.1 ms per image (10.1 images/s, ~249 MOps/s); layer 3 (5x5x32x32, 16x16x32 output) 13.1 M ops in 42.8 ms; convolution 443.4 ms -> 96.4 ms (4.6x throughput, 4.9x energy efficiency). [calc] ops = 2 x MAC (layer 1: 32x32x32x75 = 2.46 M MAC listed as 4.9 M ops): 12.35 M MAC / (99.1 ms x 216 MHz) = 0.58 MAC/cycle for the network; layer 3: 6.55 M MAC / 9.24 M cycles = 0.71 MAC/cycle.
units_and_conditions: Cortex-M7 216 MHz; 2018 library version (q7 format)
locator: Table 1 (layer runtimes), Table 2 (throughput and energy improvement), Section 5
limitations: Cortex-M7 (dual-issue) rather than M33/M4; pre-TFLM quantisation format; no absolute energy values.
relevance_to_design: Upper-end reference for SIMD int8 convolution efficiency on Cortex-M.
transferability_reason: Same 16-bit dual-MAC SIMD strategy, but the M7 pipeline achieves higher IPC than M33.
design_implication: Treat ~0.6-0.7 MAC/cycle as an upper bound for large regular conv layers; small streaming TCN layers will sit lower.

topic: LiteRT int8 quantization specification
citation: Google AI Edge. LiteRT 8-bit quantization specification (last updated 2026-05-28)
key_quantitative_findings: Weights symmetric, zero-point forced to 0, int8 range [-127, 127], per-axis (per-channel) or per-tensor; activations/inputs per-tensor int8 two's complement [-128, 127] with zero-point in [-128, 127] (asymmetric); bias int32 with (scale, zero_point) = (input0_scale x input1_scale[...], 0).
